- Landscape Seams (#2917) kept ours; TruePBR land flags unchanged.
- Cubemap sky test (#2916) made reverse-Z safe.
- Height fog (#2920) defaults taken without the Effects11 lockout.
- NativeMenu stays removed.

commit.message:
fix: release pinned GPU resources, lazy targets

VRAM pass. Session-growing leaks: Grass Optimizations kept a
NiPointer to every grass diffuse, Terrain Helper pinned every parallax
texture it had seen, the TruePBR Clone3D fork leaked a material per
clone, HiZ readback snapshots and pending NiPointers survived loads,
and LLF/Snow Cover shader resource views stayed bound after release.
Fur Shells, Interior Sun, Screenshot preview and CS Editor caches are
now freed when no longer in use.

Baseline cuts: Post Processing passes, HDR Display textures, the AMD
FSR host context, SSGI specular, SSS blur temp and Terrain Shadows
heightmap are allocated only when their feature is enabled. Grass
bucket capacity starts at bit_ceil(needed) instead of 4096.

Also: ShaderCache MakeAndAdd* keeps last-wins semantics but releases
the replaced D3D shader; HDR textures are created after Present so the
first SDR->HDR frame composites valid data; Terrain Helper clears its
extended renderer state when slots are freed; HDR blend-state and
ReverseZ caches hold a reference to their key; RAII releases for the
Effects11 and Footstep state backups; OverlayRenderer updates the CS
Editor open state when overlay rendering is skipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(snow-cover): rooftop snow and BSA textures

Sky-exposed parts of building meshes (architecture/dungeons models)
collect snow as if they were RooftopSnow units higher, gated by
Skylighting sky visibility and model height so streets, steps and
covered walkways stay clear. Adds the SnowRooftop extra shader
descriptor bit, three Snow Cover settings and bumps the feature ini
to 1-5-0.

Snow Cover worldspace textures now load through
BSResourceNiBinaryStream first, so they can ship inside a BSA, with
the loose-file path kept as fallback.
